B.K. Knights: One appearance, in 2019. B.K. Knights went 1-3 in Blue, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Teabaggers; Dug z World got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
Balz Deep: Balz Deep entered once, in 2020, and Blue was unkind: 0-3, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Spencer Torkelson were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
Banana in the Tailpipe, Holy Rollers: Four tournaments under two names entirely. They were Banana in the Tailpipe in 2022 and 2024 — 0-5 and then 1-3-1, one win in ten — and the Holy Rollers in 2023 and 2025, which went a good deal better: Green won outright in 2023 with fewer points than the side behind them, third in Pink in 2025, and a quarterfinal on both trips. Career 8-14-1, with a group title and two runs to the last eight to set against that first spell. Hot Sauce and White Zin have each beaten them twice. Nobody else in the archive has swung so far between their own two identities.
Be-Yotch-e, Please: A one-season club with something to show for it. Be-Yotch-e, Please finished 3rd in Orange in 2022 at 2-2 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of White Zin; Smug Champs got the better of them. Final ledger: 3-3. One and done.
One appearance, in 2022. Billy G.O.A.T. went 1-2-1 in Orange, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 1-2-1. One and done.
Blues Bros: One appearance, in 2023. Blues Bros went 1-3-1 in Green, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Hot Sauce; Holy Rollers got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3-1. One and done.
Bocce Balboa: One appearance, in 2024. Bocce Balboa went 1-4 in Orange, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Vandelay Industries; Long Ballz got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Boilers: Boilers entered once, in 2018, and Green was unkind: 0-3, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. They have not been seen since.
Brainerd Bergs: One perfect afternoon and two hangovers. The Brainerd Bergs were the eighth seed in 2022, third out of a logjammed Red group, and then went 4-0 in the bracket — knocking out the 5-0 top-seeded Royale w/ Cheese, then Muck Fichigan, then the unbeaten Hawkeyes in the final. They have never lost a knockout game. They have also never won another one: 1-4 in 2023, 0-5 in 2024, no bracket either year. Champions forever, all the same.
Brick Cock: A one-season club with something to show for it. Brick Cock finished 2nd in Red in 2018 at 2-1 and made the bracket. They won 2 knockout games and reached the semifinals. They got the better of Double Deuce; Flangers got the better of them. A career record of 4-2, and then they were gone.
Brothers Boor: Seven tournaments under five different spellings, and one unforgettable afternoon. Brothers Boor had never won a group — they still haven't — when they arrived at 2023 as the eleventh seed, third out of their own group, and then knocked over Sister Swap, Loose Meats, The Big LeBocce and Don Cuzzi to lift the thing. It remains the lowest seed ever to win it. The rest of the ledger is honest journeyman work: 23-18-2 overall, 6-4 in brackets, and a long-running beating from White Zin, who have faced them five times and won four. Proof you don't have to top the table to take the prize.
Brownkowski: One appearance, in 2022. Brownkowski went 2-2-1 in Yellow, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 2-2-1. One and done.
Bushwood: One appearance, in 2025. Bushwood went 1-4 in Blue, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Sparty Devils; Hot Sauce got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Chi'Bocce: One tournament. One trophy. Chi'Bocce turned up in 2019, finished 1st in Blue at 4-0, and walked out of the bracket with everything. Four knockout wins, no losses, and a name on the trophy that nobody can ever take back. Mustache Riders were among the sides they put away. Never came back to defend it. Didn't need to.
CooCoo 4 Coconuts: CooCoo 4 Coconuts entered once, in 2025, and Pink was unkind: 0-5, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Brothers Boor were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
Covid Cowboys: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Covid Cowboys won Green in 2020 at 2-0-1. They reached the quarterfinals. Trash n Stache were one of the teams that saw them off. A career record of 2-1-1, and then they were gone.
D-Boccery: Three tournaments under two spellings, with a very good middle chapter. D-Boccery went winless in 2020, then returned in 2024, finished second in Orange at 3-2, beat Hot Sauce in round one and reached the quarterfinals. 2025 undid a fair bit of it: 1-4 and bottom of Yellow. Career 5-10 with a single knockout win. When they're on, they're a problem.
Del Bocce Vista: Three tournaments across two spellings — the 2020 board wrote them down as 'Bel' — and a semifinal to their name. Del Bocce Vista made the bracket in 2019, won Yellow in 2020 and reached the last four, then went 3-2 in 2021 without qualifying. A 10-7 career record and a group title in the bank. Not a long stay, but a good one.
Dickens Cider: Three tournaments, one quarterfinal. Dickens Cider went 1-3 in 2019, then had their moment in 2020 — 2-1 in Yellow out of a three-way tie, into the bracket, past The Seekers in round one, out to Muck Fichigan in the quarters. A 1-4 in 2021 brought the road to an end. Career record 5-9. White Zin and Trash n Stache each beat them twice and were never beaten back.
Don Cuzzi: A veteran of six tournaments whose best day came late. Don Cuzzi won their group unbeaten in 2018 and went out in the quarterfinals, then wandered through some lean years until 2023, when they took second in Orange on a head-to-head tiebreak, knocked out the unbeaten top-seeded White Zin, and went all the way to the final. They have slipped since — 1-4 in each of the last two years. The overall 14-17-2 undersells a side that has beaten the Hawkeyes twice. The Big LeBocce remain the bogey team.
Double Deuce: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Double Deuce won Red in 2018 at 2-1. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Flangers; Brick Cock got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-2. One and done.
Double Doink, The Mesh: Three tournaments and four names, and not one of them stuck. They were Meshed Up in 2021, Return of the Mesh in 2023 and Double Doink in 2025, with an All Meshed Up somewhere in the unrecorded years for good measure. The bocce has been steadier than the branding without ever being good: 1-4, then 2-3, then 2-3 again, no group better than fifth, and the bracket has never once been in reach. Career 5-10. Jeff Polk and Mayank Srivastava have spent more effort on the marquee than on the scoreboard, and both have played for other clubs since.
Dug z World: A one-season club with something to show for it. Dug z World finished 2nd in Blue in 2019 at 2-2 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of B.K. Knights; Chi'Bocce got the better of them. Final ledger: 3-3. One and done.
Flangers: A one-season club with something to show for it. Flangers finished 3rd in Red in 2018 at 2-1 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of Hurricane Ditka; Double Deuce got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-2. One and done.
Get Leid: One appearance, in 2022. Get Leid went 1-4 in Yellow, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Ghetto Ballers: A one-season club with something to show for it. Ghetto Ballers finished 2nd in Red in 2023 at 3-1-1 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. Hot Sauce were one of the teams that saw them off. A career record of 3-2-1, and then they were gone.
Glory Holz: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Glory Holz won Yellow in 2025 at 4-1. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of D-Boccery; Hawkeyes got the better of them. A career record of 4-2, and then they were gone.
Goldylichs: One appearance, in 2023. Goldylichs went 2-2-1 in Red, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Vandelay Industries were among the sides they put away. Final ledger: 2-2-1. One and done.
Grand Lakes: One appearance, in 2023. Grand Lakes went 1-4 in Blue, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Muck Fichigan; Sister Swap got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Gumby Dammit: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Gumby Dammit won Yellow in 2024 at 5-0. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Brainerd Bergs; Hawkeyes got the better of them. A career record of 5-1, and then they were gone.
Guns n Rollers: Four tournaments, two trips to the bracket, and not one knockout win to show for it. Guns n Rollers opened with an 0-3 in 2020, improved steadily, and made the field in both 2024 and 2025 — losing in round one each time. Those back-to-back 3-2 group campaigns are the best work of their career. The Hawkeyes are the nemesis: three meetings, two defeats. The breakthrough is out there somewhere.
Hawkeyes: The only club to answer the bell at all eight recorded tournaments, and the first name engraved on the trophy once the records begin. The Hawkeyes swept their group in 2018 and rode it all the way home, then spent the next six years being very good and never quite getting back — a quarterfinal exit as defending champions in 2020, and a 2022 campaign that produced the only unbeaten card in the field and still ended in defeat in the final. Three group titles, 7-4 in the bracket, and semifinal appearances a full six years apart. Guns n Rollers have seen more of them than anyone and have the worst of it. Two clubs were here before the records start, but nobody has a fuller attendance sheet.
Here 4 Beer: One appearance, in 2023. Here 4 Beer went 1-4 in Blue, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Grand Lakes; Brothers Boor got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Hide Your Moms: A one-season club with something to show for it. Hide Your Moms finished 2nd in Blue in 2024 at 4-1 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Laces Out; The Seekers got the better of them. A career record of 5-2, and then they were gone.
Hilltoppers: A one-season club with something to show for it. Hilltoppers finished 3rd in Blue in 2021 at 3-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of Vandelay Industries; Smug Champs got the better of them. Final ledger: 3-3. One and done.
Hitchhikers: One appearance, in 2025. Hitchhikers went 2-3 in Yellow, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Mistress Irrelevant; Guns n Rollers got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-3. One and done.
Hot Sauce: Four tournaments of almost. Hot Sauce reached the bracket in three of them and got as far as the 2023 semifinals before the run ended. They have never won a group and have never finished better than second in one. The record sits at 12-11-2 — the very definition of a side you don't want to draw and don't much fear either. Sparty Devils have taken two of their three meetings. Always in the mix, never quite in the picture.
Hung Like a HorsePower: Hung Like a HorsePower entered once, in 2021, and Red was unkind: 0-5, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Dickens Cider were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
Hurricane Ditka: Hurricane Ditka entered once, in 2018, and Red was unkind: 0-3, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Flangers were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
I Can't Decide: A one-season club with something to show for it. I Can't Decide finished 3rd in Red in 2020 at 1-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of Guns n Rollers; The Seekers got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
Inches From Glory: One appearance, in 2024. Inches From Glory went 1-3 in Yellow, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Brainerd Bergs; Guns n Rollers got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
Joanie Loves Bocce: Seven tournaments on the books, two more before anyone was writing it down, and one of the great runs this event has ever seen. They were in the field for both 2016 and 2017, neither of which survives on paper, and they have not missed much since. In 2021 Joanie Loves Bocce came in as the twelfth and final seed and knocked over John-John, the Richard Simmons Exp. and the unbeaten top-seeded White Zin before falling in the final — the deepest run any last seed has ever managed. They took their group outright in both 2024 and 2025. The Smug Champs are the great rival: four meetings, honours dead even. Still hunting that first trophy.
John-John, Inc: Three tournaments, one group title, and a habit of running into White Zin. John-John went 1-2 as newcomers in 2018, then won Yellow in 2019 at 4-1 and marched to the semifinals — the best day they had. In 2021 they went 4-1 again and racked up 97 points, more than anyone else in the tournament, finished second, and were bounced in round one by the last seed in the field. Both of their career losses to White Zin came in brackets. They went out at the top.
Kase-Kare-Cock: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Kase-Kare-Cock won Green in 2019 at 4-1. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Brothers Boor; Dickens Cider got the better of them. A career record of 4-2, and then they were gone.
Keen on Christ + Blue Balls: One appearance, in 2022. Keen on Christ + Blue Balls went 2-3 in Yellow, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 2-3. One and done.
Laces Out: Two tournaments in Blue, two mid-table finishes. Laces Out went 2-2-1 in 2024, squeaked into the bracket third, and lost in round one to Hide Your Moms — the very side that had already beaten them in the group. A 2-3 in 2025 left them outside. Career 4-6-1.
Loh Hang Balls: A one-season club with something to show for it. Loh Hang Balls finished 3rd in Orange in 2023 at 3-2 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Long Ballz; Don Cuzzi got the better of them. A career record of 4-3, and then they were gone.
Long Ballz: Three tournaments, one good one. Long Ballz finished bottom of Orange in 2023 at 1-4, then returned in 2024, went 3-2, made the bracket and reached the quarterfinals before White Zin ended it. A 2-3 season in 2025 followed. They are 7-10 all time and have beaten Brothers Boor twice. White Zin, on the other hand, have never lost to them.
Loopers: A one-season club with something to show for it. Loopers finished 3rd in Yellow in 2019 at 3-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of Wildcat; John-John, Inc got the better of them. Final ledger: 3-3. One and done.
Loose Meats: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Loose Meats won Red in 2023 at 4-1. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Vandelay Industries; Brothers Boor got the better of them. A career record of 4-2, and then they were gone.
Mag Dick: A one-season club with something to show for it. Mag Dick finished 3rd in Green in 2025 at 2-2-1 and made the bracket. They won 2 knockout games and reached the semifinals. They got the better of The Seekers; Don Cuzzi got the better of them. A career record of 4-3-1, and then they were gone.
Magnum: One appearance, in 2021. Magnum went 1-2-2 in Green, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Rolling Stones; Muck Fichigan got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-2-2. One and done.
Merman: One appearance, in 2022. Merman went 1-3-1 in Blue, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 1-3-1. One and done.
Mickey the Mitcher: Two tournaments, one bracket, no knockout wins. Mickey the Mitcher went 2-2-1 in 2022, made the field as the nine seed, and lost their opener to the eventual champions. A 2-3 return in 2024 wasn't enough to qualify. Career 4-6-1. They did beat Joanie Loves Bocce once, which is more than most can say.
Mistress Irrelevant: One appearance, in 2025. Mistress Irrelevant went 2-3 in Yellow, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of D-Boccery; Hitchhikers got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-3. One and done.
Moist Baguette: One appearance, in 2024. Moist Baguette went 1-4 in Blue, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Banana in the Tailpipe; The Seekers got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Muck Fichigan: Four group titles in five appearances — only White Zin has more — and still no trophy, though they have come within one game of it twice. Muck Fichigan went 3-0 in 2020 and reached the final, only for Trash n Stache to take it off them. They won Green in 2021 and Orange in 2022, reaching the semifinals in both. In 2025 they went 4-0-1, the only side nobody could beat all tournament, marched to the final again, and ran into White Zin. Their .726 is bettered only by White Zin themselves. Twice a finalist, twice denied.
Mustache Riders: Two tournaments and one of the great Cinderella runs. Mustache Riders went 1-2 in 2018 and still reached the quarterfinals; then in 2019, seeded twelfth and last out of the five-team Blue group, they knocked out On Wisconsin and that tournament-best 94-point campaign, took down group champions Kase-Kare-Cock, and made the semifinals before Chi'Bocce finally stopped them. They are 6-6 all time and 3-2 in brackets. Chi'Bocce beat them twice; nobody else managed it more than once.
Noonan: One appearance, in 2019. Noonan went 1-4 in Red, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Reservations @ Dorsia; Ohiowa got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Ohiowa: A single appearance, and they very nearly took it all. Ohiowa came 1st in Red in 2019 at 4-1 and rode it to the final. They won 2 knockout games and reached the final. They got the better of Noonan; Reservations @ Dorsia got the better of them. A career record of 6-2, and then they were gone.
On Wisconsin: Two tournaments, two brackets, and the best win rate of any short-stay club. On Wisconsin went 2-0-1 in 2018 and reached the semifinals; in 2019 they went 4-1 and put up 94 points, the biggest total in the entire tournament — and were knocked out in round one by the last seed in the field. That is a cruel way to be remembered. Career 8-3-1 at .708. Came, conquered the group stage, left.
Pink Ladies: Two tournaments, no brackets, two wins in total. The Pink Ladies went 1-3-1 in 2019 and 1-4 in 2021, finishing fifth in their group on both occasions. They beat Noonan and they beat the Sparty Devils, and that is the whole ledger. Every tournament needs somebody to play against.
Reservations @ Dorsia: One appearance, in 2019. Reservations @ Dorsia went 1-3-1 in Red, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Ohiowa; Del Bocce Vista got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3-1. One and done.
Rolling Stones: One appearance, in 2021. Rolling Stones went 1-4 in Green, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Joanie Loves Bocce; Don Cuzzi got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-4. One and done.
Royale w/ Cheese: One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. Royale w/ Cheese won Blue in 2022 at 5-0. They reached the quarterfinals. Brainerd Bergs were one of the teams that saw them off. A career record of 5-1, and then they were gone.
Sister Swap: Two tournaments, two strong group campaigns, two round-one exits. Sister Swap went 3-1-1 in 2023 and 4-1 in 2024, finishing second both times — and lost their opening knockout game on both occasions. A .625 career win rate with absolutely nothing in the bracket to show for it. Brothers Boor have split their two meetings. The group stage has never been the problem.
Smug Champs: Four appearances, one trophy, and the best bracket record in the game. Smug Champs came out of the most brutal group ever assembled — the 2021 Blue four-way logjam, where a team with more points than them didn't even qualify — as the seventh seed, then beat Hilltoppers, the 5-0 Seekers and Muck Fichigan to take the title. They are 7-2 in knockout games, a rate nobody with volume can touch. Semifinals again in 2022 and 2025. Joanie Loves Bocce are the recurring foil across four meetings.
Sparty Devils: Five tournaments, and they keep coming back for more. The Sparty Devils are 6-15-3 all time and have reached the bracket exactly once, in 2025, where they lost their opening game. The nadir was 2021: 0-4-1 and dead last in Yellow. The high point was a respectable 2-2-1 in 2023. Smug Champs have played them three times and won the lot. Loyal, durable, and still waiting.
Spencer Torkelson: A one-season club with something to show for it. Spencer Torkelson finished 3rd in Blue in 2020 at 1-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of Balz Deep; Vivace do Tinge got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
Steam Punks: A one-season club with something to show for it. Steam Punks finished 3rd in Blue in 2018 at 1-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of The Bryan Adams Show; White Zin got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
Steve + Jake: One appearance, in 2022. Steve + Jake went 2-3 in Red, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 2-3. One and done.
TNT: A one-season club with something to show for it. TNT finished 2nd in Yellow in 2018 at 2-1 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of The Bryan Adams Show; Hawkeyes got the better of them. A career record of 3-2, and then they were gone.
Teabaggers: One appearance, in 2019. Teabaggers went 1-3 in Blue, good for 5th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Dug z World; Chi'Bocce got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
The Best Looking Bocce Team: One appearance, in 2021. The Best Looking Bocce Team went 2-2-1 in Red, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Dickens Cider; John-John, Inc got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-2-1. One and done.
The Big LeBocce: Three tournaments, and they got better every single time. The Big LeBocce went out in round one in 2021, reached the quarterfinals in 2022, then took Orange outright in 2023 at 4-1 with 99 points — the biggest haul anyone posted that year — before the eventual champions stopped them in the semifinals. They are 11-8 all time and 2-3 in brackets. Brothers Boor have their number, winning two of three. A short career, steeply upward.
The Boys r Back: The Boys r Back entered once, in 2020, and Green was unkind: 0-3, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. They have not been seen since.
The Bryan Adams Show: A one-season club with something to show for it. The Bryan Adams Show finished 2nd in Blue in 2018 at 1-2 and made the bracket. They went out in round one. They got the better of John-John, Inc; Steam Punks got the better of them. Final ledger: 1-3. One and done.
The M.J.s: The M.J.s entered once, in 2024, and Red was unkind: 0-5, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Joanie Loves Bocce were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
One tournament, and they owned their corner of it. The Richard Simmons Exp. won Blue in 2021 at 3-1-1. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Hilltoppers; Del Bocce Vista got the better of them. A career record of 3-2-1, and then they were gone.
The Seekers: The nearly-men. The Seekers are 25-12 all time with two group titles and one of the best win rates of any club with real mileage — and they have never won it. Six tournaments, six trips to the bracket, and a knockout record of 3-6 that tells the whole story. They went 5-0 in 2021 and lost in the quarterfinals; they went 5-0 again in 2024, reached the final, and lost that too. Vandelay Industries have never beaten them in three attempts. Somebody hand these men a trophy.
Top Gun: One appearance, in 2022. Top Gun went 2-3 in Red, good for 6th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. Final ledger: 2-3. One and done.
Trash Panda's: A one-season club with something to show for it. Trash Panda's finished 2nd in Yellow in 2019 at 3-2 and made the bracket. They won 1 knockout game and reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Wildcat; Hawkeyes got the better of them. A career record of 4-3, and then they were gone.
Trash n Stache: Three tournaments, one trophy, and the best knockout record in the game. Trash n Stache came out of a three-way logjam in Yellow in 2020, then beat Bros Boor, the unbeaten Covid Cowboys, Vandelay Industry — the side that had just knocked out the defending champions — and finally Muck Fichigan, 3-0 in their group and unbeaten all day, in the final. Five knockout wins against a single defeat. They reached the quarterfinals again in 2021 and slipped to 2-3 in 2025. And one honour is theirs alone: Spencer, the drunkest man ever to win this thing.
Trojan: Trojan entered once, in 2019, and Green was unkind: 0-4, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Joanie Loves Bocce were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
Tyson's Micropenis: One appearance, in 2024. Tyson's Micropenis went 3-2 in Red, good for 4th, and the bracket stayed out of reach. They got the better of Mickey the Mitcher; Joanie Loves Bocce got the better of them. A career record of 3-2, and then they were gone.
Vandelay Industries: Import, export, six tournaments, and one glorious afternoon. Vandelay Industries are 11-20-1 all time, the thinnest record of anyone who has shown up this often, but in 2020 they came second in Green and then knocked out the defending champion Hawkeyes in the quarterfinals before falling in the semis. That remains the high-water mark. They have reached the bracket just twice in six attempts and have never won a group. The Seekers have played them three times and won all three.
Village People: Village People entered once, in 2018, and Yellow was unkind: 0-3, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. They have not been seen since.
Vivace do Tinge: A one-season club with something to show for it. Vivace do Tinge finished 2nd in Blue in 2020 at 2-1 and made the bracket. They reached the quarterfinals. They got the better of Spencer Torkelson; Muck Fichigan got the better of them. Final ledger: 2-2. One and done.
White Zin: The greatest dynasty the B.B.G.C. has produced, and it took them nine years and one broken heart to get going. White Zin were in the field for the first two tournaments, 2016 and 2017, neither of which was ever written down; the record picks them up losing the 2018 final, after which they spent five seasons collecting group titles — five of them, more than any club in the archive — without ever getting back to the last game. In 2024 they scraped out of their own group on a four-way tiebreak at 3-2 and won the whole thing anyway; in 2025 they went 5-0 and did it again, the only repeat champion on record. They are 35-9-3 across the recorded era at .777, and they have reached the bracket in every single year the archive can account for. Brothers Boor have played them five times and lost four.
Wildcat: Wildcat entered once, in 2019, and Yellow was unkind: 0-5, bottom of the pile, and no way out of the group. Loopers were one of the teams that saw them off. They have not been seen since.
